utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we have the case called, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-83-PT, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, the appearances for the parties, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, assisted today by Tecla Henry-Benjamin, Kyle Wood, our intern Kornelis Kasper and our case manager, Carmela Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much and for the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to the Prosecution. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Ms. Quincy Whitaker we represent Mr. Rasim Delic. With us is our legal assistant, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we note the accused is enjoying provisional release. Will there be any matters in connection with that that needs to be reported?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, but no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, as the parties are well aware, this is the -- if my calculation is correct and as parties know, I'm a new Pre-Trial Judge on this case, it's the 6th Status Conference and the case has been going on for nearly one year and a half. I think the issues that have been, if you will, occupying the parties and the Trial Chamber are close to a resolution and it means that, I think, we could be able to see the pre-trial phase end with the end of this year, and I'm aware that the parties met with the Senior Legal Officer two days ago in a 65 ter conference and let me remind you that any issues that were discussed at that point, you do not need to raise here again. The way I want to proceed is just to check some of the matters regarding disclosure, first of all, and then we will go over and discuss the way forward, as it were. Let me, before that, indicate, which I'm certain that was discussed also two days ago, that the pending motion of the indictment, I had hoped to be able to inform you that the decision of the Chamber was either taken, been filed or could be filed tomorrow. I'm afraid we will have to wait until next week but I think I can assure the parties that the decision will be handed down in such good time before the recess that should any of the parties seek, request for certification, in order to appeal it I think that could be well dealt with within the normal time-frame that we have from now and until the recess. Any questions, Prosecution or Defence has on this point? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I also note for the record that that is not a matter for the trial level, that there is a pending case regarding the accused's request for material in the Blaskic case and that is being dealt with by the Appeals Chamber so that is at the moment of no concern to us. Could we then turn to where we are regarding the disclosure matters and let me say that I'm grateful for Prosecution for having submitted the status following the request done at the 65 ter Conference and I think it would be proper for you to comment and give the information which you handed over, so please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Pursuant to the request of Mr. Boas at the 65 ter Conference, we did reduce to writing as Your Honour has indicated the disclosure status to date and again at the outset I note that in cooperation with the Defence we have taken a very liberal disclosure policy and have disclosed all witness statements taken in the course of the investigation of this case, which is why there are significantly more witness statements disclosed pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii) than we anticipate actually calling at trial. Having said that, based on the information as of yesterday our records indicate we've disclosed 28 witness statements pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), that would be supporting material, we have disclosed 156 statements pursuant to 66(A)(ii) from which we will eventually determine a pool of witnesses that we will call at trial, and we have disclosed two witness statements pursuant to Rule 68(i). Again pursuant just for sake of completeness we have indicated that at this point we will call approximately 70 witnesses at trial, of which approximately 15 we would expect would be written witness statements or written testimony in the form of transcripts from prior cases. We would anticipate an approximate additional 15 witnesses by way of which we would seek to use Rule 89(F) to adduce their testimony and we would at this point anticipate the likelihood that we would be calling two expert witnesses, one dealing with military issues and one dealing with what is colloquially known as the Mujahedin issue, and depending on circumstances relating to a currently ongoing exhumation site there may be a package of forensic expertise in the form of perhaps pathologists or archeologists -- or anthropologist that is we may seek to be calling. That exhumation site was recently discovered and currently is being worked upon. So again, those -- Your Honour, at this point in time, are the figure that is we provided to the legal officer, Senior Legal Officer yesterday pursuant to his request at the 65 ter Conference held the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I let the counsel for the accused comment on this, could I ask you, Mr. Mundis, if you have in light of the number of witnesses that you now anticipate you would call, and also conditioned obviously upon the decision regarding the scope of the indictment, whether it would be possible for you to estimate in a number of months the size of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: If you haven't done that exercise I will not press you to do it but if you have, please reveal it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have in fact, Your Honour anticipated that that question may be one that would be put to us. Based on the figures and the estimates that we currently have at this point in time, and again subject to also in terms of cross-examination times, we would anticipate that the Prosecution case, as it currently exists with the currently existing indictment, would require approximately four to five months for the Prosecution phase of the case. Again, assuming that the cross-examination times were roughly the same amount of time required by the Prosecution in its direct examination of the witnesses. Again, Your Honour would be very familiar with the filings concerning the proposed amendments. Again, we don't anticipate that, were the Chamber to grant leave to amend, that that time would be significantly lengthened due to the fact that the three proposed crime bases have been the subject of prior litigation or partial litigation. So again we are looking we believe at this point in time a Prosecution case of approximately four to five months or perhaps five to seven months if the Chamber were to grant us leave to amend to include the additional three crime bases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Comments from counsel for the accused on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I take that to mean that you are in accord with the estimates that the Prosecution has done and, as far as you can view it, it's a question of the amount of cross-examination. I seem to recall that I saw that you wanted more than the double time that Mr. Mundis anticipated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I said last time, at the Status Conference, the last Status Conference, and what I asked the registry is that they be a little more realistic in assessing the time necessary for the production of evidence, and I still consider that it is more realistic to go along with the second point the Prosecution made, that their part will last five to seven months and we will certainly need the same time for the cross-examination as they take for the examination-in-chief, and in certain cases, longer. We will need more time than the Prosecution spends on the examination-in-chief and we are going to ask the Trial Chamber to give us that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, we are shooting as it were at the moving target so I don't think there is it any need at this point to try to narrow it down more. But we're looking at something around six months for the Prosecution case regardless of the outcome of the decision on the indictment, given the comments from counsel now. Could I then move it something that we haven't touched upon which is the question of adjudicated facts which obviously also would be linked to the scope of the Prosecution case? I would like to hear Mr. Mundis on this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have given this issue some thought as well and again it was briefly discussed with -- at the Status Conference or the - excuse me - the 65 ter Conference. Part of the issue here as Your Honour is well aware is that the crimes that are charged in the current indictment, the Maline/Bikosi crime base has been the subject of litigation in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case. The Kamenica camp part of the indictment has never been litigated here before. The Hadzihasanovic case is under appeal or a number of issues from that case are under appeal so that the potential for adjudicated facts with respect to the indictment as it currently stands is rather limited, although there could be some that go to the general context or the general armed conflict on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the relevant time periods. But the specifics concerning the actual crime base itself, in terms of adjudicated facts, we believe are rather limited with respect to the indictment as it currently stands. Again, if we were to be talking about an amended indictment based on those three additional crime bases there would be in the Prosecution's submission significant number of adjudicated facts and/or prior testimony that would be the subject matter of -- of litigation that we would be putting before the Trial Chamber for its consideration. But the number of adjudicated facts that would be applicable because of the nature of the indictment and the crimes alleged therein is rather limited in this case. To move to the next issue of agreed facts, that's certainly something that I believe both of the parties are interested in, in pursuing in good faith, once we have the issue of the indictment finalised. We probably can then sit down on some of the issues and reach some agreements with respect to agreed facts once the indictment is finalised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Mrs. Vidovic, comments on this? I'm particularly interested to hear your supporting comments regarding the spirit of openness with which you address the question of agreed facts in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point in time, it is too premature to speak about adjudicated facts for the reasons presented by my learned colleague of the Prosecution, since the Hadzihasanovic appeal is pending and in view of the fact that a decision has not been made yet with respect to the request made to amend the indictment. As far as the second question is concerned, agreed facts, we will certainly cooperate with the Prosecution. It is in the interests of the Defence to see what facts can be agreed, and go to trial with agreed facts as far as possible and wherever possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Vidovic. I take heart in that approach. I have understood from the 65 ter Conference that the Defence at this point do not consider to put forward any special Defence submissions. Is that correct? I'm referring now to Article 67(A) or Rule 67(A), I should say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, it seems that we have explored sort of where we are at the moment, and as indicated we could then look ahead. And my understanding is that there has hitherto not been a formally adopted work plan for this case and for reasons that parties are well aware of. I think the time has come now to adopt a work plan, and the times were discussed at the 65 ter Conference, so the dates that I will now put forward I hope will meet with the expectations of both counsel for the Prosecution and counsel for the Defence. So let me then first -- and this is obviously subject to if there are any major changes following the decision forthcoming on the scope of the indictment. There could be revisions. But these dates are factored in such a way that they should be neutral in relation to that decision but one never knows so that's why I put that caveat in. The -- let's start then with the continued disclosure of 66(A)(ii) which could follow obviously from the indictment if there is leave to amend it the way the Prosecution seeks. The Chamber would expect the Prosecution to disclose that material not later than the 29th of September this year. At the same time, i.e. the end of September, the 29th of September, the Prosecution should put forward its suggestion as to agreed facts and the parties, if possible, come to an agreement as of the same date. The same goes for adjudicated facts. The 29th of September is then significant for three things, continued disclosure, 66(A)(ii), agreed facts, and adjudicated facts. The disclosure under Rule 68, i.e. exculpatory, is obviously ongoing and by comments from counsel for the accused, seems to be satisfactory. We note that at present, counsel for the accused do not anticipate to put forward any notification of alibi or special defence. Should that change, the date for that submission should also be the 29th of September. The pre-trial brief, which is the important phase obviously in the pre-trial stage, from the Prosecution according to Rule 65 ter (E) and expert reports under Rule 94 bis should be submitted not later than the 31st of October this year. The response then from the Defence, i.e. the pre-trial brief for the Defence, under Rule 65 ter (F) should be submitted not later than the 1st of December, 2006. We will obviously continue to have Status Conference, and the next one would then be envisaged under there work plan to be sometime in October. That will give us an opportunity to review submissions from the Prosecution and where we are on the issue of agreed facts, end of September. And obviously then any unclarity as to the scope of the indictment should have vanished, if it doesn't vanish within the next couple of days. Any questions from counsel regarding this work plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just one issue of clarification, Your Honour. With respect to the remaining material that's required of the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 65 ter, and I'm speaking specifically of a witness list and an exhibit list, I note that Your Honour was silent as to those points and I take it from that that we are not, pursuant to this work plan, being asked to provide a witness list or an exhibit list within this time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: We are two time periods. We have the 29th of September obviously and that should be fulfilled, and then what is not there should obviously be in the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So that's the point I'm asking for clarification. Do you want an actual exhibit list and a witness list as part of the pre-trial brief that's due on the 31st of October?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I think that's preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, any comments, questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. With this work plan now in place, I think the substance of what we are here for today has been dealt with and it only remains for me to ask whether counsel would like to raise any other matters that we haven't touched upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that being the case, we now stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
